note: Pes cavus and related foot deformities are consistently documented across patients with SPTAN1 loss-of-function variants presenting with distal hereditary motor neuropathy or distal weakness.

evidence.text: A Chinese proband with a de novo heterozygous SPTAN1 nonsense variant presenting with distal hereditary motor neuropathy exhibited pes cavus on neurological examination at age 21.

source.title: A novel de novo SPTAN1 nonsense variant causes hereditary motor neuropathy in a Chinese family
source.quote: Neurological examinations at the age of 21 showed pes cavus,

evidence.text: Among participants harboring heterozygous SPTAN1 loss-of-function variants, foot abnormalities occurred in 10 individuals, specifically presenting as pes cavus in 5 of 20.

source.title: Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in SPTAN1 cause an early childhood onset distal myopathy
source.quote: Foot abnormalities were present in 10 participants and ranged from pes cavus (5/20) or pes planovalgus (1/20) to distal arthrogryposis (4/20).
